questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To get the Erasmus Grant and an English-speaking country.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: Easy

questions.answer: Intro week and help from the visiting Student Office

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hard. Recommendable to find something beforehand.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's hard to find accommodation off campus - especially during the Autumn semester because of the Festival in Edinburgh. Other than that, when you finally find accommodation it's quite nice, because you don't have to share kitchen and bathroom with 5-7 other people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The Visiting Student Office sends you a link, where you can see what courses are available. From that link, you also pick what courses you would like to take. It is recommended that you pick some extra courses, in case your first choice is not available.  After you have submitted the formular, you get a confirmation email from the Visiting Student office, informing you whether your chosen courses have gone through or you have to choose other available courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Visiting Student Office was helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2 of the 3 courses I wanted. I submitted the formular just 2 days after I received the link - which was late if you want the popular courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose your courses as soon as you get the link. Or else, you can risk that you do not get all the courses that you want - especially if that course is a high-demand course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I liked EU law and Environmental law. I did not like International Criminal law, because of the Teacher and because of the Reading list. The professor did not reply to any of my mails, and the way the course is built does not make sense compared to how the exam is. In the seminars, we discussed different cases we had to prepare before the classes. For instance, what rule applies to this case etc. The problem is, however, that the exam is an essay where you don't solve a case. Rather you have to critically assess a statement - and the students are not prepared for that in the classes. 
Another thing is that the chapters we were required to read were not listed in the readings. Rather, only the books were mentioned - and we had to find the relevant chapters for the seminar. This made it hard to keep up.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was 3rd year courses: Honours.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was different. The style of teaching was focused on the student discussions rather than a teacher just explaining the rules. Here, they also focus more on that we learn something rather than just preparing us for the exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EU Law Honours I: Foundations - LAWS10226
 Environmental Law - LAWS10235
 International Criminal Law (Honours) - LAWS10236

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend EU law and Environmental law because of the exam form which in both courses consist of a Video-presentation and an Essay. It is managable.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices are like the Danish prices. Transport is cheaper. Food is a bit cheaper. Groceries are the same.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many clubs you could join. So all kinds of activities were available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club - you can find friends there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the City Centre. Book a trip to the Highlands and Isle of Skye. International Student tours is recommended. Explore the food - there are very good restaurants and they offer student discount in many places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs, quiz nights etc. The University has an "Events App" where you can see different events. Talk with your classmates and invite them to a coffee - it is really easy to make friends because people are so nice and approachable - you just have to talk with them. Start with your classmates ;)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing. It was actually more nice to live here than Denmark. People are so nice.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness of the Scottish People.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find accommodation beforehand, be aware of scammers in the process, enjoy.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Public transport is so easy to use here. Especially trams.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To explore the Scottish Nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding accommodation off campus - you have to do a lot of things: Apply for Council Tax exemption, buy Wifi, speaking with Energy companies to pay the bills etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
